query: My conversational search assistant still gives poor later-turn answers after I manually rewrite each query to stand alone. I need research that investigates why resolving the query's context is insufficient. Limit the search to papers first posted on arXiv before 2021, with a university affiliation in China.

I am screening retrieved financial discussions for injected content, but harmless informal posts keep getting flagged. I need an empirical study of how the detector's training examples can cause these false alarms. For the source, require a paper first posted on arXiv before 2026, with only university affiliations.

For text-guided medical segmentation, I want to use masked reconstruction as additional training supervision. I need a method with experiments showing how aggressive image masking affects segmentation quality. The paper must have at most 8 authors and have been first posted on arXiv before 2025.

A paired image-text pretraining corpus is expensive for us to build. I need a model with controlled experiments showing how sharply its retrieval performance changes when that corpus is reduced. For the source, require a paper first posted on arXiv before 2024, with at most 3 authors and at least one company affiliation.

After grouping clinical rating scores into fewer levels, my longitudinal model predicts individual markers better but diagnoses worse. I am looking for a probabilistic modeling study that examines this tradeoff. Only consider papers first posted on arXiv before 2024, with at least one university affiliation.

I already have a small convolutional image classifier and a larger Transformer. Their accuracy ranking reverses with training-set size; I need an ensemble strategy with experiments covering both small and large datasets. Please restrict the search to papers first posted on arXiv before 2024, with a university affiliation in the United States.

When my language model already knows an answer, a fixed reasoning budget wastes calls. I want a confidence-sensitive search method with an empirical cost-accuracy analysis. Only consider papers first posted on arXiv before 2025, with an author affiliated with University of Science and Technology of China.

My sensitive attributes mix numbers and categories. I need a method to enforce demographic parity during neural-network training, without splitting people into fixed subgroups or training a predictor of their sensitive attributes. For the source, require a paper first posted on arXiv before 2024, with a university affiliation in the United States.
